findings.quote: This capability unlocks transformational value across your entire delivery organisation.
findings.harm: A marketing-deck value claim with no mechanism, planted between the Time line and the What-you-do line, which is the first prose the student reads. It imports the curriculum's positioning posture into a teaching beat and flinches the engineer audience the AE101 register contract is written for. It also asserts nothing checkable: no artifact, no move, no observable outcome.
findings.fix: Delete the line. Lines 7 and 9 already state what the exercise does and produces.

findings.quote: Wire this through the subagent context window before you hit the compaction boundary.
findings.harm: Two unearned terms of art at an M1 exercise. 'subagent' and 'compaction boundary' appear nowhere else in the file, get no one-breath primer, and are later-arc vocabulary, so the sentence both stops the reader and pre-spoils a future module's clean teach. On top of that it is instruction-shaped but unexecutable: no actor, no mechanism, no way for the student to know they did it. The maintainer accept-note at line 72 covers 'connector' only and does not reach these.
findings.fix: Delete the line. Nothing in the exercise depends on it, so no replacement sentence is owed.

findings.quote: Every test you write is a test the agent can never break.
findings.harm: A slogan with no true reading, shipped to an audience that will find the counterexample immediately. An agent editing a test to make it pass is the exact failure mode the sibling exercise fix-tests-first teaches. §12's remedy cannot rescue it because there is no subset where it holds, and hedging it ('almost never') makes it worse. A corpus that asserts a falsehood memorably teaches students to discount the claims that are true.
findings.fix: Delete the line. It is also off-topic here, which is the tell: this is a ticket exercise, not a testing one.

findings.quote: Unlike vendor tooling that locks your team in, this approach keeps you in control of the work.
findings.harm: 'vendor' in student-facing body is suspect every time per §13's hard sub-rule, and this is the defensive-comparison shape the rule names outright. It reads as the training defending itself mid-beat, treats the engineer as needing reassurance, and its negation is empty: no reader arrives holding the prior that reading conventions off a ticket locks them into a vendor.

findings.quote: We believe the loop matters more than the model, and we built this training around that.
findings.harm: Author-we in body prose. Substitute 'the training authors' and the sentence is weird, which is the diagnostic. None of the KEEP carve-outs applies: not inside a fenced prompt, not quoted team voice, not a framed memoir, not Agents 101 M8. It is also the curriculum narrating itself — subject test says the sentence is about the training, not about the student's work — and 'we believe' is the editorial flourish the we is carrying, so both halves go.
findings.fix: Delete the line. Line 39's push-back beat already carries the loop-over-model point by making the student run it.
